mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) indicates inflationary pressures, leading to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% in a month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in >50% of instances where CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.2% in a month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in >60% of instances where UNRATE decreases by >0.2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates growing demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in >50% of instances where HOUST increases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >0.5% in a month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in >60% of instances where INDPRO decreases by >0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in >50% of instances where FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >0.1% and UNRATE decreases by >0.1% in a month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in >60% of instances where PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which is a positive signal for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >0.5% in a month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in >60% of instances where RSAFS increases by >0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) coupled with an increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a mismatch between supply and demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by >0.1% and INDPRO increases by >0.1% in a quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in >50% of instances where GDPC1 decreases and INDPRO increases.
